title: Surrounded by Beauties, What’s Wrong with Me Keeping Male Concubines?
author: Cang Yu Zhi Jian
synopsis:
Xie Qingyu has transmigrated, becoming the licentious and untamed Princess Zhaohao in a novel, only to find out she won't last three chapters. 
As cannon fodder, she meets her end by ramming into a pillar after the male lead usurps the throne; Xie Qingyu smiles: Wealth and glory are sought amidst danger, she wants both power and handsome men! Taking advantage of the male lead's lack of momentum, she hires an assassin to kill him, but how did this assassin end up crawling into her bed?!

Feng Huai: Offering my pillow? If Your Highness fancies it, it's only natural.

The redeemed, frail young attendant's gaze shifts, only to viciously snap someone's neck a moment later!

Fuyao: This princess showed me great kindness, and I have nothing to repay it with save for this mortal skin. Would Your Highness disdain it? The black-bellied male lead showing signs of whitewashing? She raises her hand and strikes with a blade, directly...

chapters.title: Counter-Kill on a Rainy Night
chapters.content:
[Your Highness... the Prince Consort is still kneeling before the bed...]

[Your Highness... am I or the Prince Consort more formidable...]

[Your Highness... speak...]

………………&………………

Xie Qingyu snapped her eyes open, her entire body convulsing.

It hurts, it hurts so much, it hurts like hell...

Candlelight flickered in the dark room, and an unpleasant, foul odor permeated the air.

A water-soaked leather whip lashed down viciously, ripping fabric asunder, and yet another bloody welt abruptly surfaced.

Kang Fuhai raised a hand to stroke her cheek, finally resting it on her neck, and said with a sinister tone, "Why must you be disobedient... This servant will have to punish you properly."

Xie Qingyu broke out in goosebumps. The howling wind and pouring rain outside couldn't drown out the wild pounding of her heart within her chest. Her mind was a complete blank. By the time she came to her senses, that shrill voice had abruptly stopped.

Fresh blood gushed forth. Kang Fuhai collapsed to the ground, his hands clutching desperately at his throat, a gurgling sound rattling in his windpipe. Those gloomy eyes stared fixedly at her, and within moments, he breathed his no more.

The heavy stench of blood in the room assaulted her nostrils. Xie Qingyu's gaze flickered, landing on the dark red yesa robe, and she muttered under her breath, "It's fine, they're just paper cut-outs anyway." Yet her hand, gripping the shard of porcelain, trembled uncontrollably.

...

The rainy night was as dark as ink. The palace walls of the Forbidden Garden were already mottled and peeling, exposing the crumbling bricks beneath.

Before long, a faint candlelight flickered to life, barely illuminating the space within arm's reach.

On a dilapidated bed, a boy of about ten years old was running a high fever, his face flushed crimson as he muttered incessantly.

A cold cloth pressed against his scorching forehead. The boy laboriously forced his eyelids open, his tightly knitted brow relaxing slightly as he whispered a very soft "Elder Sister," before sinking back into a delirious sleep.

Xie Qingyu pulled back the damp quilt to let the heat dissipate, then gently rolled up the boy's sleeves, using her fingertips to massage his Quchi and Hegu acupoints.

This "golden egg" must not be compromised under any circumstances!

Seeing the boy gradually grow calm, she finally let out a slight breath and began to calmly evaluate her current predicament.

The good news: She had transmigrated. A lifetime of wealth and glory awaited her, and being surrounded by handsome men was no longer a dream.

The bad news: The original owner's life was tragically short, and her death was gruesome.

Ramming into a pillar and dying, blood splashing three chi, what an understatement of misery!

Xie Qingyu shivered involuntarily, her skull throbbing with a dull ache. She raised a hand to press her brow, inwardly lamenting that trashy dramas shouldn't be accepted, instant karma was truly a thing.

A few days ago, her manager had handed her a web-novel script. The title didn't matter; it was adapted from some male-oriented harem novel. She played one of the villainous female supporting characters who wielded towering power but suffered a desolate end, ultimately dying by her own hand after the male lead ascended the throne.

And just before her transmigration, she had been earnestly "studying" certain grand scenes in the original work.

Meow the damn it all, she was only making a cameo as a minor supporting character, why did she deserve this kind of retribution!

How did the book put it again?

She was doomed.

As a reader who skipped plotlines ten lines at a glance and only read the smut word-by-word, she honestly hadn't retained much of the plot.

However, the original owner's identity and background were quite clear to her:

Princess Zhaohao, raised in the Inner Court since childhood, tyrannical, arbitrary, headstrong, and pathologically licentious. Her estate was swarming with male concubines, numbering in the hundreds of handsome men and beautiful women...

Thinking of this, she pursed her lips, barely able to suppress the wildly curving corners of her mouth as her pretty face gradually twisted into an expression of excitement and perversion.

Suicide? Absolutely out of the question.

If anyone was going to be ended, it would be the male lead.

Xie Qingyu slapped her own thigh hard, damn it all, she had transmigrated too early!

The next second, she grimaced in pain.

Her freshly changed plain robes were already seeping blood. The whipped wounds throbbed with sharp pain, as though someone were dragging sharp nails viciously across her flesh.

Xie Qingyu lowered her gaze to stare at her palms, her eyes a turbulent undercurrent of darkness.

Neither too early nor too late, she had actually arrived right on time.

However, the most urgent task at hand was how to protect this "golden egg" and walk out of the Inner Court alive.

She wracked her brains to recall the plot she had read, finally unearthing a sliver of useful information:

In the spring hunt of the seventh year of Yongsheng, the crown prince met with an accidental, severe injury and died without recovery. The emperor, consumed by fury and grief, suffered a relapse of an old illness, and his imperial health deteriorated steadily from that day onward.

The clan of Noble Consort Xiao seized the opportunity to press step-by-step, petitioning for the reinstatement of a crown prince. The Empress of the Middle Palace bore no sons, and the remaining imperial princes were either unsuitable in status or mediocre in talent, prompting the Empress's faction to finally remember Xie Qingyu and her younger brother who were struggling for survival in the Inner Court. The following spring, they managed to leave the Forbidden Garden.

Right now, absolutely no one cared whether this pair of siblings lived or died. Four full years was enough time for the grass on her grave to wither and flourish several times over.

Moreover, she had just killed Kang Fuhai, the grand eunuch of the Inner Court. Before dawn broke, the imperial guards would likely arrive to make arrests.

Two imperial offspring abandoned in the Forbidden Garden, completely ignored by all, what hidden cards could they possibly possess?

chapters.title: The First Gleam of Dawn
chapters.content:
"Elder Sister, I don't want you to go... Don't leave, Elder Sister!"

Xie Su, who had yet to be granted a formal title, bolted awake, his hands grabbing wildly in the air before finally clutching Xie Qingyu's sleeve, scrambling up to embrace her tightly.

Having her arm, covered entirely in whip scars, gripped with such force instantly triggered a sharp pain, causing Xie Qingyu to draw in a sharp, quiet breath.

As if scalded, Xie Su withdrew his hand abruptly, his voice carrying lingering terror: "Elder Sister..."

Perhaps due to some lingering instinct remaining deep within this body, Xie Qingyu almost reflexively extended her arms, gathering Xie Su's still-trembling form into her embrace, her voice softening involuntarily: "Little Yu, be good. Elder Sister is right here, it's alright."

Xie Su raised his head, his gaze colliding abruptly with the glaring, bright red strangulation mark on Xie Qingyu's neck, his pupils shrinking violently.

His hand rose halfway, hanging suspended in mid-air, before he forcefully suppressed the surging heartbreak, clenched his fists tightly, and pulled it back.

"That old dog!" A hoarse, low growl squeezed through clenched teeth, wrapped in a viciousness utterly mismatched with his tender, youthful features: "I will surely tear him... limb from limb!"

On a desolate, rainy night, this intensely venomous curse uttered by a child under ten years old exuded a heart-stopping chill.

Xie Qingyu said nothing; she merely reached out to gently pry open his tightly clenched fists, whose tender palms were already indented with deep red nail marks. Staring at those wounds, she spoke in a tone so calm it bordered on indifference: "There's no need. I've already sent him on his way."

A violent jolt wrung Xie Su's heart. His gaze snapped up, tracing the young girl's face inch by inch. The moment their eyes met, he froze for a fraction of a second before hurriedly averting his eyes.

"What?" Xie Qingyu raised an eyebrow slightly. "Is Little Yu scared?"

"No..." Xie Su suddenly grasped Xie Qingyu's hand, his voice cold. "I only ache for Elder Sister's hand, staining itself with blood... for such a filthy thing."

~~~

The rain stopped as dawn broke, and the drizzle pattered lightly against the crumbling roof tiles of the Forbidden Garden.

The imperial guards finally forced open the gates of the Forbidden Garden.

Uniform footsteps shattered the puddles accumulated in the courtyard, sending out ripples of chaotic rings. Beneath dark red robes the color of blood were black brocade boots embroidered with cloud patterns.

Xie Qingyu stood quietly in the courtyard, fine misty rain dampening the hem of her skirt.

He Song, the commander of the imperial guards, rested a hand on the hilt of his waist sword and strode forward. Beneath his lion-patterned helmet, a pair of sharp, sword-like eyes swept coldly and indifferently around, finally resting on the seemingly fragile young girl before him.

"Someone committed arson and murder in the South Alley last night. Kang Fuhai, an inner court eunuch, had his throat slit with a porcelain shard and died on the spot... Investigations show that you appeared in the South Alley around the third watch, acting suspiciously and bearing heavy suspicion! This official is under imperial decree to investigate this case. Men..."

He furrowed his brow and shouted in a deep voice, "Take this woman down!"

"Lord He, such words are laughable." A crisp voice rang out abruptly. Xie Qingyu looked at him calmly. "The Inner Court is a heavily guarded, critical area. How could a frail woman like myself wander freely back and forth through it? As for murder and arson... that is even more baseless."

Rainwater gathered from the eaves, dripping down in a steady patter.

"Silver-tongued and deceitful!" He Song's expression darkened slightly, clearly lacking the patience to spar with her. "Whether it is baseless or not, once you enter the imperial prison, the truth will out!" Refusing to waste any more breath, he raised a hand and waved it down.

At the command, the surrounding imperial guards immediately stepped forward. Metal armor plates clashed, emitting a crisp, echoing sound as they closed in step by step.

Xie Qingyu's gaze narrowed, and she rebuked with a scowl, "Audacious! I am a scion of the Great Zhou imperial house. How dare you act so lawlessly!"

Several guards were startled by her sudden, stern shout. Their steps faltered, hesitation and doubt clouding their faces, and for a moment, no one moved forward.

He Song lowered his eyelids and said coldly, "The daughter of a disgraced concubine, what talk of lawlessness! Take her down!" He gave the sharp order once more, shattering the momentary stillness.

Oh well, playing the intimidation card failed!

The imposing wave of imperial guards came and went like the tide, their heavy footsteps grinding against people's hearts as they faded into the distance.

Xie Su curled himself tightly behind a corridor pillar, his entire body soaked by the wind-driven rain, his face as pale as paper.

What does it mean to be of supreme imperial blood? What does it mean to be a golden branch and jade leaf?

Their mother had always taught them over and over again not to harbor resentment, not to foster hatred in their hearts.

Yet now, their mother was dead.

And now, they were taking away Elder Sister...

How could he not resent? How could he not hate?!

That raging fire of hatred was on the verge of incinerating his remaining reason! He wanted nothing more than to rush out of this cage this very second, rush before that man, and demand of him: Over all these years, did you ever think of us even for a single moment?!

If he and Elder Sister had been born mere commoners, perhaps they wouldn't have had to bear this seemingly prestigious yet utterly ridiculous bloodline, being wantonly trampled and humiliated in this dark corner by those incomplete, filthy, and base creatures!

Stains of dark red had somehow smeared onto the vermilion pillars, and outside the high walls, the wind and rain shook crimson blossoms down from the trees.

chapters.title: Respectable in Appearance, Beastly Within
chapters.content:
The rain cleared.

The sunlight shone brilliantly, and the azure sky was washed clean, adding a touch of vitality even to the dreary imperial palace.

"'A sudden breeze stirs the lotus leaves, spilling quicksilver across a green jade plate', such fine scenery, only to have its tranquility disturbed."

Slender fingers brushed lightly over the clear lotuses in the stone vat. Consort Ning curled the corners of her lips, casually plucking off a few petals and letting them drift down onto the water's surface.

"The imperial prison is foul and filled with gloomy qi. With Your Ladyship's thousand-gold body, why bother going there personally?" Wanchun advised in a low voice, pulling a silk handkerchief from her sleeve to carefully wipe away the slight flower juice staining the gaps in her nails.

Consort Ning raised her hand, her gaze landing on the clear, lustrous jade bracelet gracing her wrist. She gazed at it intently for a moment, ultimately saying nothing.

Outside, the morning sun rose, radiating boundless brilliance that chased away the last lingering traces of the post-rain gloom. Yet deep within the imperial prison, it was a world of sunless, biting cold, sunlight here was the most distant of pipe dreams.

In the narrow, cramped ice-chamber, bone-chilling air permeated, condensing into white mist. Breathing it in mixed with the foul air stung one's lungs with pain.

Xie Qingyu huddled in a corner, trembling uncontrollably. Her drenched plain robes clung tightly to her body, and her lips were dyed a bruised purple.

"My lord, she still hasn't uttered a single word," a jailer bowed, reporting in a low voice to the outside, his voice sounding exceptionally muffled in the confined space.

He Song set down the cup of tea, which had long since grown lukewarm; the condensation on the cup's surface dampened his fingertips. "Bring her out. Light the charcoal braziers."

"Yes."

Within moments, several braziers burning with fierce, roaring charcoal were set up in the interrogation room. The crimson charcoal blocks crackled, radiating intense heat that warped the surrounding air, creating a stark contrast to the biting frost of the ice-chamber just moments before.

Stunned by the sudden wave of heat, Xie Qingyu broke into a violent fit of coughing, her chapped lips cracking and oozing blood.

Collapsing to the ground, she felt as though the blood throughout her entire body had instantly come alive, darting wildly beneath her skin. It felt as if countless ants were gnawing at her, simultaneously aching and itching. Even the slightest movement felt like being pierced by ten thousand needles, utterly unbearable.

Bah, what a respectable-looking beast, he certainly wasn't holding back when it came to torturing people.

She held grudges fiercely!

If reinforcements didn't arrive soon, she really wouldn't be able to hold on.

"The hour is still early. After the span of a cup of tea, this official will add two more braziers, and then two more after that. The imperial prison has thirty-six kinds of punishments; we have a long time ahead of us."

Having removed his armor, He Song looked to be around twenty years of age, with refined and handsome features, even carrying a scholar-like aura. Only those eyes were as cold and sharp as ice, inspiring awe and dread.

Large beads of sweat rolled down from her forehead. The clothes on her body dried only to be soaked through again, leaving mottled sweat stains.

Xie Qingyu propped herself up on the ground with both hands, looking past the narrow doorway toward the calm figure seated outside. She suddenly pulled at the corners of her mouth and chuckled, her voice dry and hoarse: "Officer, going to such lengths to torture a young woman like me, does it bring you some sort of pleasure?"

The fingertips resting on the long table paused slightly. He Song lowered his gaze, his eyes falling upon her sweat-slicked, disheveled face, his tone remaining flat: "Did you kill the person? Did you set the fire?"

"So what if I did? So what if I didn't?" Xie Qingyu gasped for breath. "With you conducting such torture by interrogation, Officer, you've already made up your mind. What need is there to care whether I confess or not?"

Flickering candlelight illuminated the fourteen-year-old girl, her frame not yet fully grown. Crouched on the ground, she looked frail and shattered like a wild blade of grass about to be crushed at any moment, yet deep within her eyes flickered the fierce, jade-shattering pride of mutual destruction.

The scorching, suffocating heat made one's heart fretful. He Song tugged at the collar of his inner garment, his gaze cold and sharp as it swept over her. Suddenly, a very slight, ambiguous sneer curved the corner of his lips.

"Is that so?"

He leisurely stood up, his slender fingers hooking the long sword on the table as the cold scabbard slowly pressed against her scorching skin.

Xie Qingyu shivered violently. That freezing sensation sparked a tremor across her burning body; she clenched her palms so tightly that her fingernails nearly bit into her flesh: "Officer, what is the meaning of this?"

The scabbard exerted no pressure; it merely used the momentum to nudge open her disheveled collar slightly. Beneath the deliberately wrapped fabric collar, a purplish-red bruise was shockingly exposed, the shape of fingerprints distinct and clear.

"This..." He Song's gaze locked onto the mark, his voice dropping low. "How do you explain this?"

How to explain?

Xie Qingyu almost wanted to roar internally; this damn thing was evidence left behind when Kang Fuhai, that dead pervert, went crazy on drugs and accidentally choked the original owner!

She simply struggled violently, raised her hand, and yanked open her collar. A vast expanse of bruises, stretching from her slender collarbone down to her thin shoulders and back, was instantly exposed to the scorching air and dim light.

Those weren't just finger marks; they were crisscrossing whip scars, new overlapping old, in shades of deep purple and dark red, shocking to the eye.

"Officer oversees the imperial guards, with eyes and ears reaching everywhere, could it be you didn't know?" She drew a breath, her chest rising and falling violently from agitation, yet her voice carried a bizarre tone of mockery: "That bastard bullied me for losing my power and being in distress, daring to commit offenses against his superiors and subject me to arbitrary abuse. Even a thousand cuts wouldn't appease the hatred in my heart..."

She paused, pulling her clothes back together, and actually let out a low laugh. Lifting her head to look at He Song, unadulterated hatred burned in her eyes: "Speaking of which, Officer just gave me some truly wonderful news... dying was letting him off too lightly!"

The scabbard at his fingertips seemed to sink slightly.

He Song gazed at her for a moment, no fluctuations visible in those cold and sharp eyes. He slowly withdrew his hand, uttered not a single word, and flicked his sleeves as he walked away.

Upon reaching the outer chamber of the interrogation room, an imperial guard was already waiting. Seeing him emerge, the guard immediately cupped his fists in salute and reported in a low voice, "My lord, this subordinate has verified that Kang Fuhai was of poor character, frequently abusing palace servants in his South Alley residence, and the one from the Forbidden Garden was among them. Recently, his licentious habits flared up again, and he grew addicted to Floating Light Powder, frequently harassing palace maids. Within this month alone, six female corpses, all covered in wounds, were carried out from his quarters..."

At this point, the guard paused slightly, raised his head to quickly glance at He Song's expression, and continued: "According to investigations, yesterday the one from the Forbidden Garden ran a high fever, and she had no choice but to go to Kang Fuhai to beg for some medicinal herbs. Who would have thought that fellow would be so bold as to attempt... illicit defilement. It stands to reason that she might have killed him by accident while resisting."

He Song stood silently in place, his eyes closing slightly.

Flashing through his mind was that clean, decisive cut on Kang Fuhai's corpse, one that was almost fatal with a single strike. Even after being scorched by fire, it failed to mask the killer's ruthlessness.

How could a frail young woman with no strength to truss a chicken accomplish such a feat?

Yet if it wasn't her, who else could it be? Or rather... what unknown secret was hidden within all this?

He Song steadied his mind. When he opened his eyes, they had returned to absolute calm. He instructed, "Lock her up for now." After a brief silence, he added, "No more torture."

chapters.title: Meeting an Old Acquaintance
chapters.content:
Outside the Imperial Prison, the sun shone brightly.

Consort Ning slowly stepped down from her palanquin and, leaning on Wanchun, walked inside.

An inexpressible, bone-chilling cold permeated the prison. Wanchun furrowed her delicate brows, drew a snow-white handkerchief embroidered with intertwined lotus patterns from her wide sleeve, and gently waved it in front of her before gracefully bowing to He Song. "Lord He, Consort Ning is deeply troubled and anxious, yearning for the offspring of an old friend. Might I ask you to accommodate us?"

He Song cupped his hands, bowed in return, his attitude respectful yet tinged with difficulty. "Consort Ning is of noble birth; I fear it is hardly suitable for you to venture into danger."

Consort Ning seemed to have anticipated this. Her gaze swept over the gloomy corridor, and she said softly, "Such a small matter is hardly worth disturbing the Imperial carriage. I hope the Lord can understand my heartfelt sincerity."

With the words already at this point, He Song nodded. "Please do as you wish, Your Grace!"

Consort Ning raised her brows slightly, her gaze shifting to the side.

"Thank you, Lord He!" Baishao understood implicitly. With a wave of her hand, palace attendants efficiently helped Xie Qingyu out of the dim cell.

A moment later, a delicately maintained, henna-stained slender hand, pinching a silk handkerchief carrying an elegant and refined fragrance, slowly lifted Xie Qingyu's chin.

Xie Qingyu lifted her eyelids to look at the woman before her in magnificent court attire.

Adorned in kingfisher feathers and green gauze, she wore Southern Sea sharkskin worth an inch of gold per piece, and her shoes were studded with priceless Northern Sea pink pearls.

With an immortal posture and jade-like complexion, radiating brilliance as she moved, she possessed a peerless elegance. She was truly worthy of being the person in the book who enjoyed twenty years of unwavering favor and could stand toe-to-toe with the Empress Dowager/Successor Empress.

Upon seeing the appearance of the person before her, a flash of extremely complex emotion crossed Consort Ning's eyes, but it vanished as completely as it came in the span of a breath. She sighed softly, her vermilion lips parting slightly. "In the blink of an eye over the years, Ah-Yu has grown up like this!"

Xie Qingyu did not miss the fleeting attachment at the bottom of the other's eyes. She blinked her eyelashes gently, and when she opened them again, those clear eyes were steeped in sorrow and reliance. "Consort Ning... Ah-Yu missed you so much... When Mother was alive, she often said that if not for your repeated covert care over the years, Little Yu and I... would probably never have survived to this day..."

The young girl's complexion was pale, like a white camellia after the rain; even having weathered the storm, she possessed an added vulnerability that evoked pity.

Consort Ning's gaze flickered slightly, her fingertips holding the silk handkerchief tightening unconsciously by a fraction, and her voice carried a trace of hoarseness. "I... what I could do was merely a humble effort. In the end... in the end, it caused you to suffer."

Xie Qingyu brimmed with tears, shaking her head forcefully. The tears rolled down with the movement, leaving clear traces. "To be able to be with Mother and Little Yu, Ah-Yu never felt that was suffering, but... but Mother, she..."

Mentioning the deceased Consort Hui, her throat choked with emotion, and her sadness was beyond control. "Before Mother left... she was still constantly thinking of you!"

These words were like a fine needle gently piercing the heart. The face of Consort Ning, which always maintained a harmonious and gentle composure, finally failed to suppress a flash of astonishment and trance.

She... doesn't she hate me?

After a long time, she seemed to pull herself away from distant memories, her voice so soft it was almost like a whisper, carrying hesitation. "Consort Hui... Sister... did she... leave any last words?"

Hearing this, Xie Qingyu lowered her eyes slowly, hiding the cold mockery that instantly flashed across the depths of her eyes.

Last words? Not a damn word.

In the original host's clear and painful memories, although Consort Hui had a proud and aloof temperament, her mind was the most meticulous and sharp. How could she possibly harbor any lingering attachment to someone who had long ago betrayed their past friendship and even caused her and her children to fall into a desperate plight?!

Yet when she raised her head once more, what she said was: "'Parting in death, we swallow our sobs; parting in life, our sorrow is constant. An old friend enters my dream, showing me our long remembrance.'" Before she finished speaking, her tears had already stained her lapels.

Consort Ning's long eyelashes trembled violently. The silk handkerchief she had been gripping tightly in her hand slipped away quietly at some unknown moment, fluttering down onto the dirty ground, yet she remained completely unaware.

Those memories buried deep in her heart and deliberately forgotten suddenly surged forth.

"A-Yu, look at these four-square palace walls; they frame the sky so small, and the days are so terribly uninteresting. You say, how wonderful it would be if neither of us had been chosen to enter this palace in the first place... Ah, but if that were the case, would we never have met? I suppose that wouldn't do either..."

"A-Yu, come look! This is a painting of an iron-eating beast I had someone find from outside the palace. Don't you think it looks cute and utterly docile? Don't be fooled by it, though; the book says this creature is immensely strong, and when it throws a tantrum, even iron cages cannot hold it..."

"A-Yu, everyone in this deep palace wears a mask. Only in your company do I faintly feel that there is still a living person residing within my shell, rather than a puppet wearing a title..."

The woman who was once bright, vibrant, and whose smile could illuminate gloomy years had her brilliance ground away bit by bit in this man-eating place, ultimately being completely buried here.

And herself...

Consort Ning lowered her eyes slowly, an extremely bitter self-mockery inevitably spilling from the corners of her lips.

She clearly resented her, yet facing this similar face, the heartache in her heart was so ridiculously poignant!

Looking at Xie Qingyu, she said softly, "Don't be afraid... I will save you and get you out."

"Consort Ning, I knew it, only you were truly sincere to Mother. Little Yu and I have only you to rely on." Xie Qingyu raised her trembling hand, using her tattered sleeve to wipe away the continuously welling tears, smoothly and completely concealing the deep, cold sarcasm and understanding hidden at the bottom of her eyes.

With someone as intelligent and perceptive as Consort Hui, knowing full well that the sufferings of herself and her children were merely engineered by Consort Ning's covert intentions, a final phrase of never meeting again in life or death was already the utmost completion of their youthful friendship.

~~~

chapters.title: Waiting for a Long Time
chapters.content:
Bright moonlight poured down like a waterfall, gilding the stern palace walls with a desolate silver rim. In the dead of night, a black figure draped in a cloak hurried along the palace path, light-footed, and vanished into the heavy iron gates of the Imperial Prison in an instant.

Snap!

In the gloomy cell of the Imperial Prison, Xie Qingyu slowly opened her eyes. Her gaze landed on the waist of the newcomer, and she then raised her brows slightly, drawing a faint smile.

"Waiting for a long time!" Her voice was hoarse, yet it sent faint ripples echoing through the cold, chilly air.

"Is that so?" Baishao stopped outside the cell, using the flickering light of the wall lamp to carefully size up the person before her, a trace of appreciation flashing in her eyes.

What a flower-among-moonlight sort of young woman. Although her thin, pale face could not be called stunningly brilliant, one could tell from the brightness between her brows that she was a crystal-clear, exquisite girl.

What a pity, born at the wrong time.

"Consort Ning and Consort Hui are truly sisterly in their affection, actually willing to step foot into the Imperial Prison for your sake." Baishao sounded as though she were lamenting, though her tone carried something thought-provoking.

Currently, the inner court was divided into three factions, the situation delicate.

Although Consort Xiao of the Noble Consort rank no longer enjoyed her former favor, she had the Sixth Prince, who deeply won the Emperor's heart; the Central Palace held the phoenix seal and wielded supreme power, yet her knees were empty; only Consort Ning had enjoyed unwavering favor for many years. Were it not for her unremarkable maternal family and lack of heirs, even the Empress would probably have had to guard against her by three points.

Right now, she was actually willing to run about for this person. Who could say she hadn't harbored some alternative motives? After all... there was still a young prince being raised in the Forbidden Garden!

Furthermore, among the high-ranking consorts, the virtuous Consort Xian and noble Consort Rong each had a son, not to mention the Crown Prince born of the Former Empress. The position of the Central Palace was truly awkward right now.

Xie Qingyu raised her gaze, meeting Baishao's inspecting look with calm eyes. Knowing the deeper meaning in the other's words, she only said softly, "Whether our affection is deep or not, I cannot say, but there is one matter; I wonder if the Central Palace would be interested."

"Oh?" Baishao chuckled softly. The young girl before her was unruffled, seemingly unconcerned about being trapped in the Imperial Prison.

Did she really think Consort Ning could save her?

Seeing the other remain unmoved, the corners of Xie Qingyu's lips curved into an extremely faint arc, the smile carrying a hint of wickedness. "The Empress has remained childless for many years. Would you say it is the will of heaven... or human hands?"

The air suddenly froze.

Baishao's gaze darkened, the smile on her face vanishing completely, and her voice turned sharply fierce. "Audacious! Do you know what you are saying?!"

Although the Empress was a successor empress, she had entered the palace for eight years, and the matter of having no good news for so long had long since become an unspeakable taboo throughout the Central Palace. Over the past ten years, the person before her was merely a caged bird confined to the Bureau of Palace Servants (Yetang); how dare she speak such reckless nonsense!

Not to mention that the Central Palace held the phoenix seal and controlled the entire inner court, who would dare commit such treason and risk the execution of nine generations by extending their hand to the Fengyi Palace? Furthermore, as the senior-ranking matronly official of the Central Palace, she naturally guarded against everything the Empress ate, wore, and used with utmost vigilance, never having a single half-fraction of negligence.

Baishao lowered her eyes to gaze at the girl behind the iron bars, her eyes already containing biting killing intent. "Some words, if spoken wrongly, can cost you your life."

"At the end of the year, a batch of embroidery maids was punished and sent into the Yetang, and within half a month, all of them met with untimely deaths." Xie Qingyu, however, acted as though she hadn't noticed, her voice remaining calm and wave-free. "That was because someone discovered something they shouldn't have known."

Baishao naturally knew about this matter.

The embroidery workshop had made a batch of clothes for the Eastern Palace, but unexpectedly, the coiled dragon on the Crown Prince's chest had a loose thread, and the dragon's head appeared as if it had been cleanly severed. The Emperor flew into a rage, punishing everyone from the Directorate of Clothing down to the embroidery workshop layer by layer, implicating a vast number of people.

Baishao slowly straightened up, having already recovered her calm on the surface, though her slightly tightened jaw betrayed her emotions. "And then?"

"The silk and brocade imported as tribute every year have fixed amounts, and the patterns for weaving and tapestry are bound by regulations and dare not be transgressed." Xie Qingyu raised her brows slightly, candlelight dancing in her eyes. "The fabrics belonging to the Central Palace were tampered with even before they entered the palace. Those silkworm and brocade threads were soaked in medicinal liquids day after day, and after being woven into brocade, they were scented, making it completely untraceable. Day-in and day-out erosion could eventually damage one's foundation."

Baishao's eyes rippled, and she stepped forward a fraction. "Since it was untraceable, how did you come to know of it?" The shadow of the iron bars spanned between the two of them like an unfathomably deep chasm.

"Among the embroidery maids, there was a woman from Qiannan who had known the scents of medicines since childhood and had extraordinarily sensitive senses. When splitting threads, she often held the silk threads in her mouth. At first, she only felt the taste was unusual, and later, when her menstrual cycle became irregular, she realized something was wrong. Out of anxiety and fear, she even developed a kind of mental derangement, talking incoherently... and the next day, the embroidery workshop incident occurred..."

A few sparse words in the book described an unremarkable inner palace struggle; stroke by stroke, struggling beneath were dozens of innocent souls.

Xie Qingyu closed her eyes, her long eyelashes casting light, faint shadows beneath them. When she opened them again, those black-and-white distinct eyes looked straight into the depths of Baishao's heart. "Do you truly think it was all such a coincidence?"

Naturally, it was not.

The hand in Baishao's sleeve trembled slightly.

So her mistress's wish of many years, the knot about which numerous imperial physicians in the palace were at their wits' end, had actually been calculated in this manner!

At this moment, she no longer wanted to ask how Xie Qingyu came to know of these minute details.

After a long time, Baishao finally spoke, "Your sincerity... I will naturally report it word for word to Her Grace!"

~~~

chapters.title: A Long Road Ahead
chapters.content:
Two days later, the night was like ink, all was still, and the cold wind swept across the palace walls, bringing the biting chill of late autumn.

Xie Qingyu stood before the steps, reaching out to gently smooth the temple hair blown disheveled by the wind, and smiled softly. "A long road ahead, Lord He!"

He Song stood with his hands behind his back, his crimson robes billowing slightly in the night wind. The gloomy light in the depths of his eyes appeared and vanished in an instant. "The night is deep and the dew is heavy; this official will escort Your Excellency for a stretch."

"Then I must trouble the Lord." Xie Qingyu nodded. When she lifted her gaze, the mockery in her eyes completely dissipated, leaving them as clear and bright as the spring river reflecting the moon.

A yellowish lantern swayed gently in the night wind, emitting a faint glow.

Not until the vermilion gates of the Forbidden Garden were right before them did He Song halt. He turned, extended the lantern, and spoke in a clear voice. "When we meet next time, this official may have to address Your Excellency as Her Highness."

He paused, his gaze sweeping across Xie Qingyu's face. "I shall present this lantern to Your Excellency. The light of a firefly can illuminate three feet of the ground beneath one's feet. Farewell."

The copper handle still retained residual warmth. Xie Qingyu stood in place, watching that figure blend into the night.

The dark clouds dispersed, and the moonlight, like white silk, suddenly poured down. She couldn't help raising her head, letting the pure radiance wash over her face as the last trace of ripples in the depths of her eyes returned to stillness.

Skeptical? So what? In this era where imperial power supreme, she was a princess of Great Zhou, and she clung to the Empress of Great Zhou!

Before she had even reached the doorway, a figure lunged out from inside, almost making her stumble from the impact.

"Elder Sister! You're finally back!"

Xie Pi's arms tightly locked around her waist, his entire face buried in her lapel. The boy's slender frame trembled like a withered leaf in the wind, and his muffled sobbing came through. "I thought... I thought..."

Xie Qingyu was pushed half a step back by the impact. She raised a hand to gently pat his spine, involuntarily softening her voice. "Little Yu, let go quickly; Elder Sister is going to be squeezed so she can't catch her breath."

Xie Pi hurriedly loosened his grip a fraction, yet still refused to let go, his fingers tightly clutching her sleeve. "Elder Sister, I never want to be separated from you again..." His voice carried the panic of a startled bird.

Mother was already gone; if she were to lose Elder Sister as well... he didn't dare to think.

Xie Qingyu lowered her eyes to catch sight of the other's pale face and reddened eye rims in the moonlight, knowing he certainly hadn't slept peacefully for a single moment these past few days. Her heart softened, and she raised a hand to gently pinch his cheek. "Alright, Elder Sister will always stay with you."

This was, after all, the golden thigh of her second half of life; letting go was simply out of the question.

After a moment of silence, Xie Pi suddenly asked softly, "Was it the Empress?"

Xie Qingyu was suddenly startled. "How did Little Yu know?"

"Didn't Elder Sister have Nanny Li pass a message to Consort Ning to beg for help precisely to make the Empress cast her gaze toward the Forbidden Garden?" Xie Pi raised his head, the moisture in his eyes not yet receded, but already revealing a measure of composure. "I thought... if the Central Palace hadn't made a move, matters wouldn't have been settled so quickly."

Xie Qingyu could not help but feel a chill in her heart.

Could this meticulous thought and sharp insight truly belong to a ten-year-old child? Truly precocious!

The moonlight slowly drifted across the eaves, stretching the shadows of the siblings and intertwining them together.

"Little Yu!" Her voice dropped lower, word by word. "Elder Sister has chosen a thorny path for you. From now on..."

Deep in the night, Xie Qingyu lay on the cold bed, physically and mentally exhausted, yet tossing and turning, unable to sleep.

In the darkness, all sounds were magnified infinitely: the distant night watch drums, the wind blowing against the paper windows, and even the sound of her own heartbeat seemed clearly audible.

The moment she closed her eyes, Kang Fuhai's vicious, fierce gaze stared straight at her from all directions, and the tip of her nose seemed once again to be haunted by the nauseating smell of blood in that sealed room in South Lane.

Her old wounds from the whipping began to ache faintly, a sensation that couldn't be touched yet couldn't be shaken off, an aching, numbing, itching sensation deep in her flesh, tormenting her nerves in a dense, fine web.

An indescribable melancholy choked her chest, heavy and suffocating, making it almost impossible for her to breathe.

Xie Qingyu abruptly sat up.

No! How could she allow her willpower to be shaken so easily?

Step back, and it was an abyss of ten thousand zhang, smashing to pieces! Since she had come, there was no reason to be cowardly!

I do not know how much time passed before her tense nerves gradually relaxed, and the soft, even sound of breathing finally arose.

Just as she was sinking into light sleep, the bedroom door was pushed open a crack without a sound.

A thin, small figure stepped barefoot into the room by the moonlight, moving with utmost care without making a single sound.

Xie Pi slowly squatted down by the bedside, curled up, and quietly gazed at Xie Qingyu's sleeping profile. The moonlight traced out her fatigued contours; even in her sleep, her brows were slightly furrowed.

The anguish in his eyes could no longer be concealed, almost overflowing.

His elder sister had a cold and withdrawn temperament, not even showing much intimacy toward Consort Hui, yet she kept all her warmth for him.

Consort Hui called her "Ah-Yu," so she called him "Little Yu"!

He reached out a thin, pale hand, suspended in mid-air, trembling slightly. In the end, he did not dare to let it fall, fearing he would disturb her peaceful sleep.

A single tear rolled down his long eyelashes without warning, dropping silently onto the cool brick floor.

"Elder Sister... I will listen to your words, very, very obediently..."

He leaned forward, gently pressing his forehead against the edge of the bed, murmuring softly, "You promised me, you are not allowed to break your word either."

No matter what, absolutely, you must never leave me again.

The moonlight flowed silently, enveloping the boy's slender back in a cool, silvery glow.

chapters.title: Clouds Clearing to Reveal the Moon
chapters.content:
Kang Fuhai, the Grand Eunuch of the Imperial Household Department, consumed by greed for Fuguang Powder resulting in mental derangement, deliberately committed arson and slashed his neck to end his life. He resented the majesty of Heaven and committed a heinous crime. Let him be beheaded to serve as a warning. Those in his clan aged thirteen and above shall be executed, and his remaining relatives exiled for three thousand miles.

Just two short sentences brought that murder and arson case to a close.

The gates of the Forbidden Courtyard remained shut.

Not until the rich fragrance of osmanthus completely overpowered the stale stench of the Forbidden Courtyard was that door, which they had almost stared through, finally pushed open slowly.

Li De, the Emperor’s personal head eunuch, holding a roll of bright yellow imperial edict, walked in slowly. He was around forty years old, his face fair and beardless, his brows and eyes holding just the right amount of propriety and warmth, leaving not a single flaw to be picked.

"By the mandate of Heaven, the Emperor decrees:

'Having well mastered internal governance, she is fittingly deserving of special glory. We confer upon you, the Fifth Imperial Daughter, a cautious heart and a gentle, exemplary standard. Your womanly virtue is without blemish, and your reputation shines brightly even while dwelling in confinement. Emerging from the noble lineage of the imperial bloodline, you are matched with a distinguished household. Possessing the esteemed status of the imperial genealogy, you shall jointly assist the ancestral state. The omen of the phoenix is fully in accord, and official robes are fittingly bestowed. For this, We enfeoff you as Princess Anping and bestow upon you a golden booklet. Modest in maintaining fullness, may you ever strengthen the blessings of elevating your lineage; noble yet thrifty, may your reputation for properly managing a household endure forever. Fail not in graceful deportment, and long receive generous emoluments. Respect this!'"

The phrasing was parallel and ornate, exceedingly magnificent. She only understood the most crucial sentence, enfeoffed as Princess Anping.

"Congratulations to Your Highness for dispersing the clouds to see the moon, and reaching the extreme of misfortune only for good fortune to return." Li De bowed slightly, his smile fitting.

Xie Qingyu supported the imperial edict and slowly rose: "Thank you, Head Eunuch Li."

Li De lowered his head and continued: "His Majesty has another oral decree. Mindful that the Ninth Imperial Prince is young, he specially permits him to temporarily reside with you in the Lingxian Palace, and next spring, he shall move to reside in the Chengming Palace."

Considering they had depended on each other for years and lost their mother, this arrangement was an unexpected blessing.

"Anping thanks His Majesty for his profound grace."

The mottled, paint-peeling crimson palace gates closed heavily behind them, emitting a dull, creaking sound, as if sealing off a stretch of time.

Xie Qingyu’s lean spine was held straight. Holding Xie Zuo’s hand, she stepped, step by step, out of the high threshold of the Forbidden Courtyard. The bright autumn sunlight poured down, and the wind was filled with the rich, sweet scent of osmanthus.

...

The fourth year of Yongsheng, coinciding with the Mid-Autumn Festival: Imperial Concubine Meng plotted against imperial consorts and endangered the imperial dragon fetus. The Empress, furious, ordered a thorough investigation overnight, which unexpectedly implicated a case from ten years ago.

Back then, Consort Hui of the Lu clan enjoyed great favor, but on the eve of being elevated to a noble consort, she was reported for having illicit communications with a palace musician. That very musician was Tanhuahua Shen Chi, who had been betrothed to her before falling into disgrace.

In the Emperor’s thunderous wrath, Shen Chi was granted death, Consort Hui was stripped of her title and confined within the Forbidden Courtyard, and her maternal clan was demoted time and again, banished far from the capital.

Now, Imperial Concubine Meng confessed with her own lips that the matter involving Consort Hui back then was framed out of jealousy, but alas, the person was already gone.

The Son of Heaven berated her for having a heart as venomous as a serpent, making her unfit to rear an imperial princess. The Ninth Princess was handed over to Consort Shu De to raise, and Meng was demoted to the Imperial Household Department, forbidden to leave without a summons.

The monstrous waves within the inner palace, when spoken of, amounted to mere words!

How much effort the Empress expended in this, and what role Consort Ning played, Xie Qingyu did not probe.

Gauze draped over her luxurious, embroidered shoulders, He Song stood at a distant corner of the palace path, watching the grand procession gradually move away, only withdrawing his gaze after a long while.

This Highness was truly formidable.

The next morning, with the dawn's faint light piercing the carved window lattices of the Fengyi Palace.

Xie Hao, wearing a dragon robe of crimson gold, spread his arms, allowing the Empress to arrange his final crown and jade belt: "Empress, your actions are naturally meticulous, but Anping and Lao Jiu are still young after all, and... they have lost their birth mother. Their maternal family is also withered and wretched, with no one to rely upon or show consideration. I worry..."

Before the words were finished, the Emperor in his prime sighed rarely: "It was Me back then... who failed Consort Hui."

The Empress paused slightly, gently smoothing the jade beads, and gently advised: "His Majesty was also deceived by others back then. When all is said and done, it is simply that Consort Hui lacked good fortune. Your Majesty must by no means harm yourself on this account and damage the sacred health."

The Emperor was silent for a moment, then sighed: "Very well, let Me ponder this further." He adjusted his crown and turned to leave.

The attendants held their breath, filing out. In a moment, only Baishao remained standing guard in the massive bedchamber.

A sandalwood comb soaked in rose hair oil combed through clouds of black hair, emitting a rich, tranquil, and comforting fragrance. Baishao looked at the bright and beautiful woman in the mirror, and finally could not help asking softly: "Your Majesty, just now His Majesty clearly intended for you to raise the Ninth Prince, why did you not smoothly agree?"

"Intended?"

Hearing this, the Empress smiled softly, letting go of a handful of cool, smooth strands of hair. Her gaze penetrated the mirror surface, revealing a trace of faint mockery: "It was merely calculating minds pitted against one another."

Empress Xu, already past her prime, was well-maintained and still looked like she was in her twenties. Her full head of black hair was like a waterfall, graceful and dignified. A slight smile in her phoenix eyes was like a spring breeze brushing the face, poised and moving.

Baishao thought for a moment and understood, her expression changing slightly: "Was His Majesty testing you?"

The Empress raised her eyes to look at the long-withered crabapple flowers in the courtyard, a flash of loneliness crossing her eyes: "Having no sons of my own is my greatest vulnerability."

The Crown Prince was already grown with deep roots. Among the imperial concubines, the Third and Sixth Princes were both fully grown and eyeing the throne with hostility. Even the Eleventh Prince, born of Concubine Rong, was nine years old and already understood matters.

Rather than taking the trouble to raise another toddler, it was better to gamble.

If one wanted to survive in this man-eating palace, one could only tightly attach oneself to herself, and to the Xu family.

As for Consort Ning...

The Empress chuckled softly, only regretting that she had entered the palace a bit late and never witnessed that good show with her own eyes. It was truly a pity!

chapters.title: Fathoming the Emperor's Will
chapters.content:
At the third quarter of Mao hour, with dawn's light faint, Fengyi Palace was already a gathering of orioles and swallows. Fragrance curled gently in Yonghe Palace, and amidst rustling garments and flowing sleeves, jade and pearls were intertwined.

"The Forbidden Courtyard is bone-chillingly cold, and the Ninth Prince is young; I fear he has suffered much hardship," Consort Shun said with a coquettish smile, looking toward the shifting shadows in the inner room. The hair ornaments at her temples swayed gently with her movements: "In this concubine's view, it would be better to raise the Ninth Prince in the Central Palace. The Empress holds the position of Mother of the World and can just as well care for him more closely. That would also be sharing the burden for His Majesty."

She was born delicate and lovely, and having entered the palace for only two years, she was already elevated to the rank of concubine, currently enjoying the height of imperial favor. At this moment, her words carried a sort of innocent rashness, as if she were completely unaware of what kind of massive boulder she had cast down.

A soft "clatter" sounded as a teacup was set down gently.

Consort Shu raised her eyes and let out a lukewarm cold snort: "Look at that, it is still Sister Shun who grasps His Majesty's sacred heart best. Words such as discerning the imperial will and sharing the monarch's burdens, such things we would never dare to think of, let alone dare to mention!"

The smile on Consort Shun’s face stiffened slightly, and she parried blandly: "Consort Shu’s words... sound rather as if this concubine harbors some other motives."

"Not entirely." Consort Shu’s gaze shifted, her half-smiling look carrying an indescribable mockery: "It’s just that younger sister presumptuously fathoms the imperial will; aren't you afraid His Majesty will blame you? And as for this 'good intention' of yours, I fear the Empress will find it hard to accept!"

"This concubine, this concubine when did I fathom the imperial will?" Consort Shun’s expression changed abruptly, and she hurriedly argued: "The Empress is noble as the head of the inner palace; rearing princes and caring for the harem is inherently her duty and matters of course! Consort Shu need not try to frighten this concubine like this."

"Why is Sister Shun so nervous? This palace was merely speaking a couple of jokes with you." Consort Shu covered her mouth and chuckled, then abruptly changed the subject, her gaze drifting lightly toward Consort Ning at the side: "If we truly wish to speak of the sentiment of 'caring for,' Sister Ning naturally ought to be more devoted than others. After all, your friendship with Consort Hui back then was unique in this entire palace, unmatched by anyone else."

The air in the hall grew slightly stagnant.

It was true that Imperial Concubine Meng's plot against the imperial heirs had come to a settled conclusion, but Consort Meng was not a fool; how could she have blurted out matters of a case from ten years ago? If one said there were no other hands at work behind this, who would believe it!

Consort Ning sat upright, her moon-white palace attire so plain it was almost glaring. Hearing this, not even her eyelashes trembled. She only said indifferently: "The Empress possesses blessings over the six palaces, benevolent and magnanimous. How to rear a prince naturally rests upon her own sacred judgment, and there is no need to trouble Sister Shu's mind." She had no intention of entangling herself with past people, and her tone grew even colder.

Consort Shu acted as if she hadn't noticed, continuing on her own: "Sister Shun entered the palace late, so I'm afraid she doesn't know. Back then, the Twin Blossoms of Qiongyu Palace possessed talent and appearance peerless across the six palaces. That favor and splendor... Heh, not to mention this palace, I'm afraid all the sisters seated here could only gaze in despair!"

A single sentence caused all sorts of jealous, hateful, or curious gazes to land squarely on Consort Ning.

Consort Shu felt it was still not enough. She chuckled lightly, her gaze roaming back and forth between Consort Shun and Consort Ning, and leisurely added the final spark: "Looking closely today, this palace realizes that Sister Shun’s brows and eyes truly do bear two parts of a likeness to an old friend. What do you think, Sister Ning?"

These words were too vicious! Even Consort Shu De, who had kept her eyes lowered without speaking, finally raised her eyes, her deep gaze lingering on Consort Shun’s face for a moment.

Beauties might always share some similarities, but to say they looked alike; it was truly difficult to compare her to that woman who was as bright as a flame.

Yet Consort Shun, upon hearing these words, flushed red with anger and embarrassment, blurting out without choosing her words: "This concubine is young after all, able to catch His Majesty's eye. As for Consort Shu, you; it must be that you spend your nights alone and tossing sleeplessly of late, for at the corners of your eyes, it seems another fine line has grown!"

The Emperor after all was not what he used to be, and recently he was even more busy with state affairs, making his visits to the harem countable on one's fingers. Yet Consort Shun had the fortune of accompanying him on several occasions, while Consort Shu's Penglai Palace hadn't been stepped into for over a month.

"Consort Shun! You are presumptuous!" Consort Shu’s bright, beautiful face flushed with a crimson wave of anger, and fury blazed within her meticulously painted eyes.

However, that fury burned for only a single instant before she forcefully suppressed it. Why get angry with such a stupid person!

Favor was merely the icing on the cake under the weight of power; what she wanted was never these things!

Consort Shu took a deep breath, and when she spoke again, her voice had returned to an icy calm, yet beneath that calm was a bone-chilling coldness that anyone could hear: "Flowers do not bloom for a hundred days. Sister Shun would do better to care more for herself. The one thing this palace never lacks is young and beautiful women."

Consort Shun's heart gave a jolt, startled by the flash of ruthlessness in Consort Shu's eyes, but she still stubbornly twisted the silk handkerchief in her hands, her lips moving, wanting to argue further.

At that moment, Baishao, the lead maid by the Empress's side, silently turned out from the inner chamber and nodded slightly.

Consort Shu De, who had been sitting on the sidelines all along, finally spoke slowly, her tone gentle yet carrying its own weight: "Alright, you are all sisters of the same household. It's just a few words of bickering; do not mar the harmony."

Hearing this, whatever their inner thoughts might be, the crowd lowered their heads in assent. The atmosphere in the hall eased slightly as everyone adjusted their attire and stood up to respectfully welcome the Empress.

"I could hear you talking quite lively from the inner room. Since that is the case, why not tell it to me as well?" The Empress spoke indifferently, yet no one dared to respond.

The hall plunged into sudden dead silence. Those who had been arguing fiercely moments before now all held their breath with lowered heads.

After a long while, a light snort came: "If you all feel you have too much leisure on your hands, go to Baohua Temple to copy scriptures, pray for blessings, and calm your minds. It will spare you from standing here in Yonghe Palace like marketplace shrews trading barbs, pointlessly losing the dignity of the royal family."

"This concubine knows her wrong, please Empress, spare your anger." The crowd hurriedly bowed.

"Rise, all of you. Matters concerning Lingxian Palace are not your place to meddle in. In all things, His Majesty holds his own sacred judgment."

Her current position was delicate, with countless eyes from the court and harem staring at her. She truly did not wish to overly entangle herself in the Ninth Prince's affairs and draw attention from all directions.

However, someone was unwilling to let this matter be lightly brushed aside.

"What the Empress says is entirely true, but Princess Anping is after all already fourteen, gradually understanding human affairs. Though the Ninth Prince is a full younger brother, men and women are separate; living together in Lingxian Palace for long will I fear run counter to ritual and propriety. The rules of the royal family after all cannot be lightly discarded."

The one speaking turned out to be Consort Zhen. She was always aloof and seldom participated in these disputes, but no one expected her to speak up at this moment, directly contradicting the Empress's face.

The Empress sat loftily upon the phoenix throne, her expression unchanged as she gazed steadily and calmly at Consort Zhen, slowly saying: "Although it may not strictly accord with propriety for a brother and sister to live together in Lingxian Palace, Anping and the Ninth Prince grew up in the Forbidden Courtyard and lost their mother. The two depend on each other, sharing a deep bond. To forcibly separate them now would be heartless, and I fear it would cause the imperial offspring to be frightened and unsettled. In this matter, His Majesty also pitied their early loss of parents and personally granted them temporary residence together. Consort Zhen... do you still have doubts about this?"

Consort Zhen met her gaze. After a moment, she bowed slightly, her posture still cold and distant: "His Majesty and the Empress have considered all things thoroughly; it was I who was foolish and overstepped my bounds."

"Since you know you overstepped, you should be even more cautious in speech and action henceforth." The Empress's expression grew gradually colder.

(Ranks of the Harem: Empress, Noble Consort/Consort Shu/Wise Consort/Capable Consort, Consort, Nine Concubines, Zhaoyi, Jieyu, Meiren, Cairen, Noble Lady, Select Attendant, Gentlewoman)

chapters.title: Bowing the Head and Submitting
chapters.content:
The concubines in the hall harbored various thoughts, and outside the hall, Xie Qingyu was likewise pondering.

In the original novel, the male protagonist entered the capital as a hostage, yet managed to stir up winds and clouds, while cannon-fodder figures like Xie Qingyu and her brother were merely chess pieces in his hands, discarded once used. In the ninth year of Yongsheng, the Emperor fell gravely ill, and with the Empress's backing, Xie Zuo was established as Crown Prince, ascending the throne in March of the following year at the tender age of sixteen.

As for the original owner, she would also begin her eccentric, unruly, and unbridled licentious schedule. Those hedonistic actions naturally drew impeachment from court officials and criticism from the world, yet the young emperor remained unmoved, even bestowing an entire province as her fief.

The original owner kept male courtesans and broke with conventions, causing all the imperial clan members to rage in fury. The Son of Heaven acted arbitrarily and willfully, sowing discord between monarch and ministers from then on, laying the groundwork for the male protagonist's successful usurpation.

Xie Qingyu exhaled slightly. Regardless of anything else, at least in the early stages, the male protagonist's and her goals were the same.

As for the future, blocking someone's path to wealth and honor is like killing their parents. Usurping the throne, you say? You'd have to ask if she agrees first!

Only, what kind of persona should she establish to make things convenient for herself?

The prison incident must have made the Empress wary of her. During this period, I'm afraid every move in the Forbidden Courtyard was under the watchful eyes of the Central Palace.

The better the little golden egg performed, the more securely the Empress placed her bet.

If she, this redundant bettor, became a variable, she probably wouldn't need to exist anymore.

"Your Highness, Her Majesty summons you and the Ninth Prince inside." The palace maid's voice interrupted her thoughts.

Waves of fragrant wind drifted within the hall, making one's heart itch.

Dozens of gazes fell squarely upon them, some curious, some scrutinizing, and others harboring undisguised contempt.

Xie Qingyu led Xie Zuo to kneel on the cold ground, bowing her head in salute: "Greetings to the Empress. May Your Majesty enjoy peace and health."

Even when kneeling to her ancestors in her past life, she had never lowered her head so deeply. Sure enough, being of lower status meant one had to bow and submit.

The young girl in resplendent garments was slender and small, which only made her weak spine appear all the more fragile. On the other hand, the young Ninth Prince, despite his tender years, appeared steadfast in mind with upright brows and eyes, truly a good piece of timber.

If he were a fool, he wouldn't be worth the trouble of her scheming.

The Empress withdrew her gaze, taking in the expressions of everyone present, and said indifferently: "Still kneeling for what? Baishao, go lift them up."

"Yes." Baishao bowed slightly, walking quickly to the center of the hall to help the two of them up: "Please rise, Your Highnesses."

Xie Qingyu, however, bowed once more: "Anping expresses her deep gratitude to the Empress for discerning the truth and clearing my birth mother's name, allowing the two of us to emerge from prison."

"As the Empress of the Central Palace, I naturally cannot tolerate those with crooked hearts stirring up trouble in the inner court. Imperial Concubine Meng brought this upon herself. His Majesty, in his pity, permitted the two of you to live together; you should first follow the palace eunuchs to learn the rules, and hereafter do not make false steps or lose the dignity of the royal family."

The Empress's tone was unkind. Everyone knew that Consort Shun's words had touched a taboo of the Central Palace, dragging Lingxian Palace into the collateral anger as well. Consort Shu even gloatingly glanced at Consort Shun and let out a provocative snort.

Consort Shun, who had sought to curry favor only to earn disgust, finally shifted her gaze away from Xie Qingyu's face, feeling inwardly uneasy.

How could this matter be blamed on her?

During the Mid-Autumn banquet, her mother had mentioned to her that the Xu family intended to send another young lady into the palace, and also said the Empress had managed affairs in the palace for many years, unmatched by anyone else, urging her to be sure to ally with the Central Palace.

She thought that since the Ninth Prince had lost his birth mother and had no maternal family, why not simply raise him at her own knees. If the Xu family truly sent someone into the palace to give birth to another child, wouldn't the Empress's position become awkward?

It was all Consort Shu's fault for meddling in the middle and misinterpreting her good intentions.

"Anping will keep your teachings in mind," Xie Qingyu lowered her head and replied, a flash of a smile skimming the depths of her eyes.

Indeed, wracking one's brains could never compare to a fool's sudden flash of inspiration!

This divine assistance saved Xie Qingyu quite a bit of effort. The harem was full of hypocritical, double-dealing people; false and true, they could all just take their turns on stage.

The Empress's attitude was cold and detached, making the surrounding scrutiny all the more uninhibited.

After ten years of confinement, a discarded pawn long forgotten had actually managed to survive, yet who knew who was pulling the strings behind the scenes.

After the exchange of greetings, Xie Qingyu finally managed to recognize everyone in the hall. The beauties were charming and alluring, each with her own grace. The scoundrel of an emperor certainly had a rich romantic fortune.

Since the Emperor was scheduled to come over after morning court, the Empress kept the brother and sister behind for a meal, and the concubines sensibly dispersed. The hall instantly felt much more spacious, with only lingering fragrance curling in the air. Though the knees of Xie Qingyu and Xie Zuo ached from kneeling, they maintained their respectful postures.

The Empress idly twirled the jade bracelet on her wrist, suddenly curving her lips in a light chuckle: "I like clever people, but I do not like people who are too clever."

On the embroidered gold-woven carpet, the Empress's embroidered shoes moved silently, a massive Eastern pearl swaying gently upon the shoe surface, finally halting directly in front of Xie Qingyu.

A well-maintained hand reached out, its fingertips stained with bright red nail polish, and gently hooked her chin: "When someone is too clever, foolish thoughts are born. Do you understand?"

Xie Qingyu was forced to lift her head, her eyes suitably stained with resentment and unwillingness: "Everything today is due to Your Majesty's grace. What Your Majesty desires is also what Anping seeks. I only wish to tear those who bullied and humiliated me into a thousand pieces and reduce their bones to ashes."

A subtle scrutiny fell upon this still-immature face. After a long while, the Empress laughed noncommittally. Her gaze swept over the respectful Xie Zuo and she said indifferently: "His Majesty pities you brother and sister; from now on you should be even more cautious in word and deed. Letting favor make you arrogant is no good. Do you remember?"

"Yes, we will strictly obey Your Majesty's teachings."

Xie Qingyu lowered her gaze, yet she had no desire to be this obedient puppet.

Ten years of confinement; it was a miracle she hadn't gone mad. Now that she had attained power, she naturally had to wash away every bit of the humiliation carved into her flesh and blood.

The deeper the obsession, the easier it was to control. A princess of petty cleverness and arrogant favor would also put people at ease, wouldn't she!

chapters.title: Fickle and Callous
chapters.content:
At noon, the autumn sunlight spilled through the carved palace doors into the hall. Xie Qingyu knelt on the ground, her head lowered. Within her field of vision were the emperor’s bright gold robe hem and boots embroidered with cloud-and-dragon patterns.

She had finally laid eyes on this amorous yet fickle Son of Heaven from the original book, her imperial father.

Back then, he had been utterly devoted to the original owner’s mother. When the daughter of the Lu family first entered the palace, she was merely a fifth-rank Cairen, yet thanks to the emperor’s partiality, she was promoted all the way to the rank of Pin in less than two years.

To bring a smile to the beauty’s face, he had once ordered fresh lotuses to be transported overnight from the imperial villa, solely so she could gaze upon blooming twin-lotuses at dawn. To say her favor overshadowed the entire harem would scarcely be an exaggeration.

Yet that same favor did not prevent him from doting on Consort Ning, who was then a Meiren, right inside the palace of Consort Hui. That very day, Consort Hui had retired early due to a bodily indisposition, and when the emperor arrived, he happened to run into Meiren Zhao personally decocting medicine for Consort Hui.

The following morning, the imperial edict promoting Meiren Zhao was issued directly from Consort Hui’s main hall, turning Consort Hui into the laughingstock of the entire harem.

Even when Consort Hui was framed for illicit behavior within the inner palace, the emperor rebuked her in front of all the consorts: "The offspring of a lowly woman, how can she be fit to inherit the lineage?"

It was pouring rain that day. Consort Hui knelt upon the freezing stone slabs, letting the rain soak through her garments, yet she kept her spine straight throughout, never offering a single word of defense.

A mere few sentences were all it took to doom the original owner and the yet-unborn Xie Su, banishing them alongside Consort Hui to the Yeting, where they endured a decade of humiliation and abuse.

Such was the life of the original owner; she didn't even survive to reach the tragic conclusion written in the book.

"Your Majesty." Empress Xu’s voice pulled Xie Qingyu back from her memories to reality. "The Ninth Prince has not yet been entered into the imperial genealogy. Do you wish for this name to be drafted by the Directorate of Ceremonial, or..."

The emperor finally shifted his gaze away from Xie Qingyu and onto Xie Su's face. The small, slender youth knelt ramrod straight, his thin figure like a proud, upright stalk of green bamboo. Pondering for a moment, the emperor spoke warmly: "Let us call him Xie Su. Su carries the meaning of standing tall and straight. I hope that my son will hereafter grow into an upright and steadfast gentleman."

The outer edge of Xie Qingyu's brow twitched. As expected, it was this name.

It seemed that although the plot had been advanced, it did not affect its natural progression. A crisp breeze, pure and lustrous like jade, truly a fine name.

"We thank Your Majesty for your boundless grace." The two of them bowed once more.

Looking at the obedient and sensible children before him, a trace of guilt stirred involuntarily in the emperor's heart, and his voice grew even gentler: "I have wronged you and your mother these past years. I have already issued an edict posthumously elevating Consort Hui to the rank of Imperial Noble Consort, and in days to come, I shall make it up to you properly."

"Presuming the Lu woman has spirit in the netherworld, she too will be grateful for Your Majesty's grace," Empress Xu remarked from the side.

"Rise and speak, all of you," the emperor commanded with a wave of his hand.

The two chorused their gratitude and rose to their feet. Xie Su stealthily lifted his gaze to peek, only to be caught squarely by the emperor.

Xie Su did not resemble Consort Hui; his brows and eyes rather mirrored Emperor Zhou in his own youth. A single glance cast over carried a touch of curiosity and filial yearning, involuntarily recalling to the emperor the image of his own boyhood years.

The emperor laughed heartily, in high spirits, and turned to look at Xie Qingyu instead. Yet he found her expression cool and aloof, her brows and eyes holding a mixture of reproach and petulance, clearly blaming him.

That gaze was far too direct, causing him for a moment to shrink from meeting it.

Xie Hao could not help but recall ten years ago, when Consort Hui had brought the three-year-old princess and knelt in the rain before him, gazing at him in this very manner yet refusing to utter a single plea for mercy.

How could someone so modest and well-versed in propriety commit illicit acts with a musician? Yet he truly loathed her calm self-possession, and could bear even less the silent interrogation in those eyes.

Such an attitude was merely leaning upon his favor; this time would serve precisely to make her understand that he was the emperor, and all under heaven belonged to him; he had merely bestowed favor upon one concubine among many.

If only she had begged him, if only she would speak...

Yet that woman, until the day she died, never spoke another word to him.

As if stung by that gaze, the smiling corners of the emperor's-mouth slowly dropped: "Anping, are you perhaps harboring resentment toward me?"

"Should I not?" Xie Qingyu retorted, her voice as crisp as jade stones colliding, exceptionally clear in the silent palace hall.

"Impudent!" The empress’s brows furrowed slightly, fierce severity coloring her bright and majestic face. After all, she was someone who had never been properly tutored; she simply lacked refinement.

For a moment, the hall fell into absolute silence, save for the dripping of the clepsydra.

~~~

chapters.title: Reluctant to Scold
chapters.content:
"Your Majesty..."

The empress parted her vermilion lips, but before she could finish, Xie Hao raised a hand to stop her. He gazed fixedly at the young girl kneeling in the hall, his gaze seeming to pierce through ten years of time.

After a long while, a sigh escaped his lips: "Not only does she resemble her mother in appearance, but this temper is also exactly like hers when she first entered the palace."

The daughter, who in his memories had been as cute as carved jade, had now grown into a graceful young woman, her features filled with the shadow of her mother. His heart softened abruptly, after all, this was a child he had once genuinely loved with all his heart.

If she knew the thoughts running through the emperor's mind right now, Xie Qingyu would surely sneer with contempt.

Though people often say children cannot remember events before the age of three, the fragmentary early childhood memories in the original owner's mind were chillingly real.

Resentment or hatred, if not for these sustaining her, how could she have survived the day-to-day confinement and torment?

Yet even so, she ultimately died, on that rain-drenched night, in a cramped and foul-smelling dark room, in a place her little Yu could not see.

At this thought, Xie Qingyu's throat choked up. When she lifted her face, her eyes were already brimming with moisture, yet she stubbornly refused to let the tears fall.

"Imperial Father's words didn't count." Her voice carried a choking tremor: "You said that when A'yu grew up, you would teach me to read and write, and if I had a younger brother, you would teach him to ride horses and shoot arrows. Little Yu and I waited in the forbidden gardens for ten years; we waited for you for ten years!"

Xie Su's eye rims turned abruptly red, his frail body pressing tightly against hers as he whispered brokenly, "Elder Sister."

"And Mother." Xie Qingyu continued, every word sounding as though it were carved straight from her heart: "You once said she was the best woman in the world, so why did you throw us away?"

At this point, the tip of Xie Qingyu's nose stung, and she truly shed tears.

The departed were gone; gazing at that face extremely similar to Consort Hui's, a multitude of complex emotions flashed through the emperor's eyes, ultimately dissolving into a trace of heartache and helplessness.

"It is not A'yu's fault." His voice lowered: "It is my sin."

Baishao lowered her gaze in attendance, her peripheral vision glancing stealthily at the empress, only to see the corners of the latter's lips twitching ever so slightly, the look of mockery in her eyes flashing and vanishing.

Within the span of a breath, the empress's voice recovered its former gentleness and dignity: "His Majesty is benevolent. Why not bestow another grace to comfort the princess?"

The emperor nodded, the gaze he turned toward Xie Qingyu softening a fraction: "Very well. Whatever A'yu wants, just speak. Aside from the sun and moon in the sky, your imperial father will grant it all to you."

The emperor had numerous offspring, yet not a single one dared speak to him in this manner. To do so was surely to treat him as a father rather than a sovereign.

Yet Xie Qingyu suddenly turned away with a feigned awkward look; she was running out of ability to maintain this aggrieved expression. If she had to look at the emperor's hypocritical face a moment longer, she feared goosebumps would rise all over her.

As for rewards, though... would one hundred thousand taels of gold do? To accomplish great things, startup capital could never be too much.

Her thoughts raced at lightning speed, and she finally stated flatly: "I want a manor. If ever Your Majesty grows weary of Anping again, just let me leave the palace."

"Nonsense! You are a princess bestowed by His Majesty himself. To put on such an act, are you still harboring grievances against His Majesty?" A genuine trace of anger churned within Empress Xu’s heart.

She had originally thought this lass was playing out a brilliant tactic of retreating in order to advance, but she hadn't expected her to be truly so worthless.
