Xie Qingyu kowtowed in response, her forehead pressing against the cold floor tiles, her voice muffled yet stubborn: "Anping wouldn't dare. I'm just afraid... I; I never want to be locked away again."

As these words fell, the entire room fell dead silent.

Even the palace attendants standing on either side held their breath, lowering their heads and not daring to raise their eyes.

Xie Su also dropped heavily to his knees beside her, crawling forward two steps to tightly grip Xie Qingyu's hand, his lifted face brimming with panic: "Wherever Elder Sister goes, I go! I have already lost my mother; I cannot lose Elder Sister too!"

The boy's tear-choked words struck like a blunt blade straight into the emperor's heart.

He closed his eyes, and the oath sealed away for many years seemed to ring in his ears once more; "Were I not born to the imperial house, I would spend my days in long devotion with my love."

Past events surged forward like a tide. An emperor's heart was also made of flesh, and at this moment, it was finally drowned by guilt.

"A mere manor, even ten, I would grant you. But speak no more of leaving the palace." In the end, the emperor compromised, reluctant to scold her further.

Seeing when to stop, Xie Qingyu submissively kowtowed in gratitude: "Thank you, Imperial Father, for your grace."

This was a risky gambit.

Father and daughter of the imperial house had not met for a decade; she had braved the risk of falling out of favor once more simply to test just how much weight the talisman named "Consort Hui" still held in the sovereign's heart.

It turned out that a "white moonlight" really was useful! One was like this, and every single one remained the same.

A trace of cold mockery flashed in Xie Qingyu's lowered eyes.

~~~

chapters.title: A Tentative Probing
chapters.content:
The autumn wind blew bleakly, and the white jade windchimes hanging beneath the eaves emitted a crisp, clear tinkling sound.

Xie Qingyu sat in the pavilion, watching the palace attendants bustle in and out as a steady stream of rewards was delivered continuously into Listening Immortal Palace. If anyone else were around, she feared her laughter would shatter the rafters.

They say wealth is sought amidst danger! She was now a top-tier wealthy woman; how much better it would be if she could take these rewards back to the real world and lie flat!

Pity that there was no road back.

However, wealth without power as a foundation was merely scattered sand; it didn't even need a wind to blow it apart; it would disperse all on its own.

What she wanted went far beyond this, and she could never rely on the illusory favor of the imperial house.

Pulling back her gaze, she let it fall upon the youth beside her: "In three days, you will go to Chengyming Hall to study. By then, all the princes will gather, and scions of noble families will throng together. I fear you will encounter numerous trials. Is Little Yu afraid?"

Her voice grew exceptionally soft as she reached out to pull Xie Su’s fragile shoulders into her embrace, her fingertips gently smoothing through his slightly disheveled hair.

Hearing this, Xie Su raised his head, a pair of eyes burning brightly: "Compared to the hardship of Elder Sister guarding and protecting me for ten years, even if there are a thousand more ghosts and monsters, I am not afraid!"

"Little Yu." Xie Qingyu stared fixedly into his eyes, speaking word by word: "You are an imperial prince of heavenly blood. You do not need to compromise in everything, nor do you need to blindly endure and yield. Sometimes, taking a step back does not bring a vast and boundless sky, but rather invites others to push an inch and demand a mile."

Bits and pieces of the decade they spent together rushed into her mind instantly. Xie Qingyu understood his temperament all too well.

In the years of confinement in the Yeting, eunuchs who groveled to the high and bullied the low frequently took advantage of their isolation, often amusing themselves by tormenting Xie Su.

At first, youthful and high-spirited, he had put up fierce resistance, which only earned him a more brutal beating and several consecutive days of spoiled, stinking meals. Yet if he offered no resistance at all, those wicked slaves grew bored and escalated their cruelty, concocting even more vicious and insidious methods to torment him, invariably forcing the original owner to kneel and plead before they would stop.

Later on, he learned to be "obedient."

He would struggle with "all his might," wearing an expression of aggrieved humiliation, only to "coincidentally" be easily trampled underfoot once more to satisfy their base sense of superiority. He would listen to their mockery and laughter, shoving all his hatred and sharpness deep into the mud, hiding it in the deepest recesses of his heart.

Xie Qingyu couldn't bear to think any further. That memory, which clearly didn't belong to her, pierced her chest with a dull ache.

Cupping Xie Su's face, she bloomed into a warm smile: "Study hard. Elder Sister will come to pick you up after class every day, all right?"

"Elder Sister..." Xie Su's pupils trembled violently; a sharp, piercing pain flared unexpectedly from the depths of his heart, causing his fingertips to quiver uncontrollably.

Almost instinctively, he raised a hand to cover Xie Qingyu's hands cupping his cheeks, feeling beneath his palms the warmth he craved so deeply. This subtle intimacy was the sole solace he and his elder sister had used to cling to one another through countless freezing, desolate nights.

The sound of light footsteps drew near. Xie Qingyu swept her peripheral vision past a palace maid not far away, her gaze darkening abruptly. Yet the instant she turned around, a surprised smile had already bloomed upon her face: "Consort Ning, why have you come?"

Xie Su clenched his palms, stood up, lowered his head, and bowed respectfully: "Greetings, Consort Ning."

Leaning on a maid's arm, Consort Ning walked over slowly. Her makeup was exquisite, her attire refined, and her face bore its customary gentle smile. Personally pulling the two siblings up, she indicated for them to resume their seats: "Hurry and rise. Today... you truly suffered grievances."

Sighing softly, her gaze swept in the direction of the Palace of Earthly Tranquility (Fengyi Palace), and her voice lowered further: "The empress was displeased, but she was merely using the two of you as pawns to rap certain people across the knuckles."

With the court situation unstable, the inner harem was naturally turbulent and treacherous. Today appeared to be a case of Consort Pin lacking discretion and incurring the empress's displeasure, but in truth, it was merely a shallow, tacit probing among various factions.

Had it not been for the incident in South Lane, she would not have meddled. Yet now... watching the siblings before her, especially Xie Qingyu's excessively calm eyes, Consort Ning hesitated inwardly, the words already at her lips rolling back and forth.

"Consort Ning, today's events stemmed entirely from us, implicating you in receiving a cold shoulder at the Palace of Earthly Tranquility as well. It is the fault of both Elder Sister and myself," Xie Su said, somewhat dejected, having seen the morning's events clearly.

"Consort Ning, A'yu understands your protective intentions." Xie Qingyu took up the conversation, personally lifting the warm teapot on the stone table to pour a cup for Consort Ning: "To be able to walk out of the forbidden gardens is already a boundless grace. The grievances of the moment truly amount to nothing."

Her tone was peaceful, betraying not a trace of resentment: "Coming here now, do you have something to instruct us on?"

Taking her hand, Consort Ning spoke softly: "His Majesty is sympathetic, and already intends to select one among the high-ranking consorts to look after the two of you siblings from now on."

Pausing, a trace of complexity flitted through her eyes: "Yet... privately, I have always been unwilling for you to call another person 'Imperial Mother'..."

Their birth mother, Consort Hui, had already been posthumously elevated to Imperial Noble Consort. If someone could smoothly foster the two imperial offspring in Listening Immortal Palace, it would not merely be icing on the cake; the currently vacant position of Imperial Noble Consort would be practically within arm's reach.

With such temptation, it was no wonder the hearts of those in the harem were fluttering.

Yet she had flatly refused and even advised the emperor to temporarily shelve the notion; she had no idea how many people she had offended with this stunt!

At the mention of the deceased Consort Hui, Xie Su's eye rims uncontrollably reddened slightly, yet his tone remained exceptionally firm: "For Little Yu and Elder Sister to have Consort Ning's care is already a blessing. We want no other imperial mother... We do not need one now, and we shall never need one in the future!"

"Yet, what if it is the empress?" Consort Ning had no idea why she had asked such a question; the moment it left her lips, she felt a vague twinge of regret.

Xie Qingyu's heart skipped a beat, then she furrowed her brow slightly as if touching upon some injury. Subconsciously massaging her knee with one hand, she added a trace of imperceptible grievance to her voice: "Just now in the Palace of Earthly Tranquility... Empress made us kneel for quite a while. I fear... she never truly favored us siblings to begin with."

Xie Su did not dare show disrespect to the mistress of the middle palace, but he said with heartache: "Is Elder Sister's leg hurting again?"

Consort Ning's beautiful eyes snapped shut, her gaze falling upon the hem of Xie Qingyu's skirt.

For the Palace of Earthly Tranquility to show such a lack of restraint, did they not fear losing the emperor's face? Furthermore...

Seeing Xie Qingyu's slightly furrowed brows, Consort Ning cast aside her misgivings and hastily instructed someone to help her inside the chambers. Personally lifting the skirt hem to roll the underpants up to the knee, she was instantly startled: "How did you sustain such a heavy injury?"

Beneath the green garments, slightly red and swollen bruises were clearly visible. Consort Ning's fingertips trembled violently, her breathing halting for a fraction of a second. Such injuries...

A moment later, she snapped back to her senses: "Quick, fetch a physician!"

"Your Ladyship!" Baishao shook her head slightly. If a physician were called for this today, it truly meant trampling the empress's dignity into the dirt and offending her utterly.

Looking at the injury on Xie Qingyu's knee, Consort Ning felt a stifled knot of breath raging fiercely in her chest.

"Never mind. Bring the Jade Snow Ointment."

chapters.title: Past Sentiments
chapters.content:
In the Phoenix Palace, the twilight was deepening.

The Empress leaned sideways against soft pillows on the gold-thread nanmu couch, her fingertips twisting a peacock feather, idly prodding the chin of a red-throated thrush in a cage on the table.

The bird had been impeccably trained. Flapping its wings, it chimed out human speech in a crisp voice: "May the Empress be blessed with ten thousand fortunes, ten thousand fortunes, Your Majesty..."

Yet, no matter how many times it repeated, it was always just this one phrase.

The slight, leisurely smile on the Empress’s lips gradually faded. With a flick of her wrist, the brilliantly shimmering peacock feather was tossed lightly to the floor.

"A useless fool, can't even learn a simple auspicious greeting." She slowly leaned back against her gold-woven headrest, her gaze drifting toward the window where the horizon was already stained with a dim, bruised orange.

Bai Shao raised her eyes. The bird, which had been so lively a moment before, instantly fell silent in the palm of a palace servant.

"Your Majesty, what does it matter if a trivial thing is stupid or not!" Bai Shao bowed and stepped closer, her deft hands kneading the Empress's scented shoulders with moderate pressure as she spoke in a soft, consoling tone. "This servant saw today that the Ninth Prince in the forbidden garden truly possesses a rather extraordinary bearing."

She paused. Seeing the Empress did not look displeased, she continued, "To be able to grow up with such a calm and serene disposition in a place like that, without anyone to look after him; it shows his intellect is far from ordinary."

A very light, scoffing laugh escaped the Empress's nose. "One by one, they’ve all turned into jealous hags, each dying to snatch a piece of meat. Even Consort Zhen, who is usually the most demure of them all, now wants to stir up this muddy pool. Should I praise her for being naive, or call her stupid?"

The Crown Prince had merely been reprimanded by His Majesty and ordered to reflect behind closed doors; it was of no consequence. Even she, the Empress, hadn't truly taken it to heart, yet so many people were impatiently revealing their intentions and growing restless.

"It is simply because I bear no sons of my own." The Empress's voice dropped abruptly, carrying a hint of bitterness. "It is no wonder my father is anxious and wants to send someone in again."

Bai Shao pressed her lips tightly together, not daring to reply.

Her Majesty had harmed her constitution; in this lifetime, she would likely never conceive again.

It could only be blamed on the vicious methods of the former Empress's clan, who had laid their plots right outside the palace walls, leaving them impossible to guard against.

The Empress raised her eyes to look out the window. The sun was slanting westward, the daylight retreating. Splendid as the remaining glow might be like brocade, it was ultimately the scenery of twilight.

The Xu family's century of prominence was now showing signs of decline; the burden on her father's shoulders was simply too heavy. If he could not take a step further forward, he would only be devoured by other watchful, powerful noble clans, down to the very bones.

Over the years, sitting high upon her throne in the Phoenix Palace, she had watched coldly as the princes and princesses of the palace grew up one after another. She had not been without the thought of adopting one into her own name.

Yet deep within her heart, she ultimately desired a child sharing her own blood, one who would softly call her "Imperial Mother" and bring joy to her knees.

After a long silence, the corners of her lips slowly curled into an extremely faint smile, though it did not reach her eyes.

Since she, Xu Wanyi, enjoyed this wealth and honor, she had no choice but to fight for it. For the Xu family, and for herself.

~~~

The towering palace walls could not catch a glimpse of the setting sun, which looked like fresh blood. Fragrant golden osmanthus flowers drifted all over the courtyard, their rich scent scattered by the wind, sparse yet filling the air completely.

Consort Ning draped in a plain brocade cloak, stared at the residual glow across the sky, standing still for a long time until extremely light footsteps sounded behind her.

"Your Majesty, the wind is growing strong. Let us return," Wan Chun urged softly.

Consort Ning acted as if she hadn't heard. The sense of desolation in those beautiful eyes was exceptionally profound, enough to pierce anyone's heart with pity. After a long while, she softly said, "Let's go."

Wan Chun lowered her gaze, urging the palace servants to hurry away.

Not far away, a solitary figure stood quietly, taking in every bit of this scene before the gates of Lingxian Palace. A trace of sarcasm surfaced on a face that had been calm and untroubled.

Dusk gathered, swallowing the last shred of light between heaven and earth.

Palace lamps had already been lit within Qiongyu Palace, but it was eerily quiet. Wan Chun carefully dismissed those around her and stood guard herself right outside the inner bedchamber doors, her brows knitted with a lingering, untamable worry.

With all that had happened lately, she found herself somewhat unable to understand her master. Her mistress clearly held a great deal of resentment toward the person in Lingxian Palace, her tone turning cold whenever she mentioned them in daily life. Yet, every time over the years when she heard news that the other side was feeling unwell, she would toss and turn, unable to sleep the whole night.

And yet, as for looking after them, over all these years, it amounted to no more than sparing a few lives, and nothing more.

She still remembered that in the spring of last year, when that person truly passed away, her master had been overcome with grief, sitting alone and desolate for an entire night, before finally saying in a hoarse voice: "From now on... there is no need to report anymore."

Ever since then, it seemed as though she had truly let go, leaving that desolate forbidden garden to fend for itself. If not for the Ninth Prince having no other way out and pleading before Qiongyu Palace that day, Her Majesty would likely have forgotten long ago that an old acquaintance's orphan was still living over there, wouldn't she?

Forgotten?

Naturally, that was impossible.

Inside the inner hall, Consort Ning had dismissed everyone. She had not retired to rest; a white jade wine pot sat overturned on the table, its contents more than half gone.

With hazy, drunken eyes and unsteady footsteps, she staggered twice before abruptly collapsing onto the cold brick floor. Struggling to raise her head, she looked all around her, but the field of vision was empty. The figure lingering in the depths of her heart was gone; no matter how eagerly she searched, she could not catch even a shred of clothing.

"That's right... that's right..." She lay prostrate on the ground and began to low-laugh, her laughter heavy with a nasal tone and tears. "She must be unwilling to see me ever again..."

It wasn't like that!

Didn't you say, "An old friend enters my dream, showing she remembers my long yearning"?

You clearly missed me!

"Come out... come out and see me, just once..." Consort Ning's voice broke, carrying a pleading, weeping cadence, murmuring like a dream: "Come out!"

We promised not to fail each other in this life, never to betray one another.

"Lu Zhaozhao... I hate you!"

You clearly knew I had no desire for imperial favor, that my heart was solely set on our bond, yet the moment you were six months pregnant, you meticulously plotted and pushed me right before His Majesty's eyes!

A thousand arrows piercing the heart... a thousand arrows piercing the heart cannot compare to my pain!

The twin beauties of Qiongyu Palace... Heh, how ironic is that? A romantic tale envied by all under heaven, yet nothing more than a cage built of lies!

"I snatched your favor, why didn't you hate me? Why didn't you take revenge on me..." An irrepressible sound, half-weeping and half-laughing, spilled from her lips.

Consort Ning slowly collapsed forward onto the ground, her hands clutching tightly onto a wood carving as she whispered softly: "Why did you still put on a false display of affection toward me? Leaving me without even a thorough reason to hate you!"

The person was already gone, so naturally, no one answered.

~~~

chapters.title: The Torment of Humiliation
chapters.content:
Three days passed in the blink of an eye.

On this day, before the morning light had fully pierced the clouds, figures were already visible outside the side hall of Chengming Palace. Xie Zuo arrived extremely early. He stood alone in the corridor, his figure almost melting into the lingering morning mist.

The palace servants standing in attendance inside the hall occasionally cast glances his way, but quickly looked away. No one spoke to him, as if he simply shouldn't exist in this place.

At the beginning of the chen hour [7:00 AM], Xie Qingyu stood at the entrance of Wenhua Palace. She looked up at this imperial academy with its flying eaves and brackets and grand, imposing presence, while an inexplicable sense of ominous foreboding rose in her heart.

Surely they weren't going to make her study the Four Books for Women, were they?

If so, she would rather go mad.

Yet upon entering the palace gates, she discovered that Wenhua Palace was much more expansive than she had imagined. Not only was it clearly divided into a literary courtyard and a martial courtyard, but in the distance, there was even a fairly large parade ground.

At this moment, on the parade ground, figures of young maidens dressed in crisp riding outfits could be vaguely seen practicing archery and horsemanship, their movements filled with a vibrant youthful energy.

A few young noble ladies who had just finished their morning practice were walking together in a group, fine beads of sweat still dotting their brows. Spirited and heroic, upon hearing the commotion over here, they all turned to look, their eyes revealing undisguised curiosity and appraisal.

A female official of about twenty-seven or twenty-eight walked over briskly and bowed crisply to Xie Qingyu. She wore a dark cyan martial outfit with a leather belt around her waist, her hair meticulously coiled into a bun. Her facial features were proper and her gaze sharp, exuding an unquestionable competence and majesty.

"This subordinate greets Princess Anping." Her voice was steady, yet carried an inherent pressure. "Wenhua Palace officially commences classes sharp at the hour of maozheng [6:00 AM]. Considering today is Your Highness's first arrival, this subordinate will say no more. Please, Your Highness, be sure to keep the time in mind for the future, and never arrive late."

Maozheng? Xie Qingyu calculated rapidly in her mind; that meant classes started at six in the morning. From Lingxian Palace where she resided to Wenhua Palace, traveling by sedan chair took close to half an hour, which meant she would have to set out no later than five o'clock.

Adding the time for washing up, dressing, and having breakfast... wouldn't she be dragged out of bed at four in the morning?

Xie Qingyu's vision went black.

Back in her past life, the purgatorial high school test preparation, known as the "iron body of a high schooler", never required her to wake up this early!

Given her current frail constitution worn down by the forbidden garden, breathless after walking just two steps, no matter how diligently she studied and trained, she clearly wasn't going to amount to much. Thinking of this, she almost instantly wanted to lie flat and accept her fate.

"And here I thought it was someone important, making such a grand display."

The Third Princess, Xie Cenyin, flanked by several companions, stood not far away sizing Xie Qingyu up from head to toe. She let out a cold snort from her nose, then turned her head away and ignored her.

This attitude caused several of her companions beside her to look on with curiosity, yet they were intimidated by the Third Princess's temper and didn't dare to speak rashly.

Those selected as study companions in the palace, which of them didn't have a clever, quick-witted mind?

They had long caught wind of the rumors that this newly conferred Princess Anping was highly favored by the imperial will, granted a title even before coming of age, an exclusive favor none of the other princesses possessed.

Previously, the emperor's favorite was the Third Princess, and now that a formidable rival had appeared out of thin air, it was no wonder she was unhappy.

Meanwhile, beside the rockery behind the side hall of Chengming Palace, the atmosphere was entirely different.

"Your Highness, look at this pathetic wretch! Born with a base, spineless bone, how is he worthy of being compared to you?" A tall, robust study companion smiled ingratiatingly, using all his strength to press Xie Zuo's cheek firmly against the cold, rough ground, while resting his other leg astride Xie Zuo's back in a posture of utmost humiliation.

The Eighth Princess's brother, the Eighth Prince Xie Zhen, sat leisurely on the rockery stone, coldly eyeing the struggling youth beneath his feet. "What? Someone who would kneel to a lowly servant for a moldy piece of cake has grown a stiff spine now? You refuse to beg His Highness here for mercy?"

He didn't even need to ask around, to curry favor with him, someone had naturally taken Xie Zuo's pathetic past in the forbidden garden and embellished it with exaggerated details to amuse him!

In Xie Zhen's eyes, such a base seed should quietly rot and die in some forgotten corner, lest he dirty the imperial dignity.

Xie Zuo breathed heavily and with difficulty, his cheek pressed against the icy ground. Within his field of vision, he could only see pair after pair of gorgeous embroidered boots with complex patterns.

Seeing that he still bit his teeth hard, refusing to let out a single cry for mercy, Xie Zhen found it uninteresting. He jumped down from the rockery stone and walked up to him.

Squatting down, he teased, "A stiff spine? How about I send someone to invite your good older sister over? Have her kneel and beg for mercy on your behalf, how's that? I heard she treasures you, her younger brother, dearly. I imagine... she certainly wouldn't refuse, right?"

It was no wonder Xie Zhen was so arrogant; his uncle had just returned in triumph from the southern border, subduing unrest that had plagued the borders for a decade. His illustrious military achievements shook the court and the public, and he was soon to be enfeoffed as the Marquis of Loyalty and Bravery, bringing immense prestige and popularity to his mother, Consort Rong, in the palace where everyone rushed to fawn over her.

Unbearable, mocking laughter surrounded him. Xie Zuo felt his brain buzzing, blood rushing madly to his head. Those voices seemed to pass through a thick layer of water, becoming blurred and indistinct, leaving only the sound of his own heart beating like a mad drum, thump! thump! thump!

His A-jie... was the best person in this world! These people... these filthy things! How dare they?! How dare they mention her with such vile words!

"Ah! I'll kill you all!!"

A suppressed roar burst from the boy's throat, shrill and distorted! An astonishing, brute strength erupted from his seemingly slender frame as he fiercely flipped over the robust study companion who had been sitting on top of him!

The next moment, he had clamped his hands tightly around the other's throat! His knuckles tightened ruthlessly!

He couldn't let these words dirty A-jie’s ears, kill them all!

Kill them, and A-jie won't hear it!

Kill them, kill them, kill them all!

The crazed thought raged like a wildfire, instantly swallowing all his reason.

In just two or three breaths, the study companion whose throat was gripped turned from red to a terrifying purplish-black, his eyeballs bulging, veins throbbing wildly on his forehead as he struggled vainly, looking as though he wouldn't last much longer.

This sudden, bloody counterattack scared all the study companions out of their wits!

After a brief, dead silence, the scene instantly plunged into extreme chaos. Cries of alarm rang out, and everyone rushed forward in a panic, some trying to pry his hands loose, some pulling at him, while others even threw punches and kicks in their haste, trying to rescue their companion.

Everything turned completely upside down in a massive melee.

chapters.title: The Crown Prince’s Dignity
chapters.content:
When the Crown Prince arrived, the bricks under the corridor were already stained with blood. Deep brown and bright crimson were intermingled, spreading into a glaring, chaotic mess across the bluish-grey stone surface.

His expression darkened slightly. Before he even spoke, the aura of authority radiating from him instantly silenced the chaotic scene. Behind him, guards stepped forward swiftly, forcibly separating the crowd of people who had been brawling.

"Inside the Chengming Hall, imperial princes and study companions are brawling. This truly is an eye-opener for Gu." Xie Yu swept his gaze over the crowd. Noses bleeding profusely, garments disheveled, hair falling loose, such sights were everywhere, utterly unsightly.

His gaze finally landed on Xie Su, who was surrounded in the center.

The youth had a frail figure, his face covered in bruises. The exposed skin of his neck was crisscrossed with shocking bloodstains, his lip split open, a trail of dark red blood winding down to stain his plain-colored collar.

Only those eyes were pitch-black and blazing, devoid of fear, holding instead an almost fierce, stubborn resilience.

Xie Yu’s gaze turned sharp as he shifted it to the Eighth Prince, Xie Zhen, standing nearby: "Eighth Brother, why don't you tell Gu what on earth is going on here!"

The dignity of the Crown Prince brook no questioning.

Xie Zhen also reined in his unruly expression: "Your Highness the Crown Prince, please discern the truth. We were merely sparring and playing around, and lost our sense of measure for a moment."

Seeing this, the others scrambled to their knees, speaking in unison: "May Your Highness discern the truth, it truly was just play!"

Li Cheng, who had nearly been choked to the point of passing out by Xie Su just moments ago, finally recovered his breath.

He hurriedly flipped over, scrambled up, and knelt on the ground, kowtowing repeatedly while his voice still carried a hoarse cough: "Reporting to Your Highness the Crown Prince... Ninth Highness has just arrived and is not acquainted with anyone. We, we only had good intentions to accompany him in a bit of sparring, truly just playing around. Who would have thought Ninth Highness would take it seriously..."

A few other study companions who had previously tried to pull them apart and discourage the fight knelt on the ground, words failing them at the tip of their tongues, when the Crown Prince had already spoken indifferently.

"Is that so?" His gaze swept past Li Cheng’s ingratiating and pleading visage, the corners of his lips curling into an icy arc. "Gu will grant you a favor as well. Fang Zheng, you shall accompany Young Master Li and these few study companions to 'properly' spar."

Li Cheng’s neck instantly shrank inward, his face turning ashen: "Your Highness? Ah... Your Highness the Crown Prince, there's really no need... Ah!!"

Before his voice finished trailing off, the Eastern Palace guard named Fang Zheng closed in like a ghost, catching Li Cheng’s arm with one hand and striking the back of his knee fiercely with the other.

With a miserable scream, Li Cheng was hoisted up by immense force and hurled heavily onto the cold, hard brick floor. It produced a teeth-setting, muffled thud, instantly causing him to curl up in pain, unable to utter another complete word.

Watching his study companions being disciplined one by one, Xie Zhen’s expression shifted repeatedly between pale and ashen, until he finally couldn't help stepping forward: "Crown Prince! Do you truly intend to damage the harmony between us brothers for the sake of some irrelevant nobody?"

"Eighth Highness, those words overstep your bounds." The eunuch standing respectfully behind the Crown Prince reminded him in a low voice, his tone deferential yet carrying undeniable warning.

"When this Highness speaks, is it your turn, a eunuch, to interrupt!" Xie Zhen was in the heat of anger; without even thinking, he snapped back harshly, showing not an ounce of appreciation.

Xie Yu’s brow furrowed abruptly, his voice sinking: "A gentleman has nine concerns: in seeing, to be clear; in hearing, to be acute; in expression, to be warm; in demeanor, to be respectful; in speech, to be sincere; in handling affairs, to be reverent; in doubt, to question; in anger, to think of the consequences; in seeing gain, to think of righteousness. The teachings of the Master; you have cast them entirely behind your mind. So volatile and devoid of decorum, go back and copy the Analects: Ji Shi chapter ten times to steady your mind and learn a lesson."

Having reprimanded Xie Zhen, Xie Yu’s gaze fell once more upon the group of study companions who were now silent out of fear.

"The Eighth Prince went astray in his actions, and you, as his study companions, knew not to advise him otherwise, but instead fanned the flames on the side, simply despicable! The Ninth Prince was personally bestowed a name by His Majesty, and his name has been entered into the imperial genealogy after being reported to the ancestral temple. How dare you recklessly deride and physically assault him? Did you ever consider what crime it is to desecrate the royal family and commit offenses against your superiors?"

"Your Highness, calm your anger! Your Highness, spare us!" Their complexions turning pale, several of them knelt in panic to beg for mercy, no longer daring to offer the slightest defense.

Li Cheng was even more frightened out of his wits, earlier, he had been pressing down hard on the Ninth Prince to beat him...

At this thought, sweat poured from him like rain.

Disregarding the intense pain throughout his body, he used all his strength to crawl forward on his knees for two steps, throwing himself before Xie Su, who had remained silent all along, and kowtowed with loud thuds: "Ninth Highness! Ninth Highness! It was my mind being clouded by lard! I was wrong! I will never dare do it again! I beg you to spare me!"

If the person who came today had not been the Crown Prince, even if the Grand Tutor himself had arrived with the Eighth Prince shielding them in front, at worst they would have only received a scolding and been punished to kneel for a few hours.

Yet the one who came happened to be the ruler of the state, the future master of the realm. The dignity of the Eastern Palace would not tolerate the slightest bit of such lawlessness from them.

Since Xie Yu had intervened, naturally he would not let the matter go lightly.

He raised his hand slightly, his voice brooking no doubt: "Summon the Inner Court executioners. Every study companion who participated in the brawl today shall receive twenty strokes of the heavy staff, execution to be carried out immediately."

This punishment could hardly be called light.

Staff beatings from the Inner Court, even if the executioner eunuchs showed mercy, after these twenty strokes, these individuals would likely be unable to get out of bed for half a month.

More importantly, being punished by the direct order of the Crown Prince was tantamount to branding an extremely unglamorous mark upon their yet-unbegun official careers.

Without monumental opportunities or illustrious achievements in the future, their prospects in this lifetime would essentially come to an end right here.

Soon, the heavy thuds of the staff and the shrill screams and pleas for mercy echoed beneath the corridor.

Xie Zhen’s face was as dark as water, his hands clenched into fists inside his sleeves. Ultimately not daring to act wildly, he suppressed his full belly of anger and flicked his sleeves in departure.

That malevolent gaze made Xie Yu feel a slight chill in his heart. Wanting to seek brotherly affection within an imperial family; he had been naive.

Yet turning back to meet that pair of clean eyes, he felt his heart soften involuntarily, and he smiled: "Are your injuries heavy? When you couldn't beat them, didn't you know how to run? The one who acts tough and suffers losses is always oneself."

The injuries on the youth’s face appeared all the more ghastly, yet his gaze remained clear and stubbornly resilient. Perhaps the tenacity within those eyes had touched him, or perhaps both of them had lost the protection of their birth mothers, causing Xie Yu to naturally harbor a shred of pity for the person before him.

Xie Su, however, shook his head. Enduring the pain, he bowed to him with utmost solemnity and meticulous stiffness: "Thank you, Your Highness the Crown Prince, for stepping in to resolve the crisis."

He paused, raised his eyes, and added in a calm tone: "Actually, if Your Highness had arrived a bit later, I probably would have choked that wretch to death."

He thought to himself, since they were the ones who struck first, even if he really had choked that person to death, it should... not have required him to forfeit his life, right?

To his surprise, upon hearing this, Xie Yu not only did not reprimand him for having a heavy murderous intent, but instead was slightly stunned before bursting into a loud laugh. The laughter dispelled the previously congealed atmosphere.

"You certainly have a ruthless streak! Very well, follow Gu to the Eastern Palace to change into a clean set of clothes, and let the imperial physician apply some proper medicine for you."

He reached out and ruffled Xie Su’s hair, which had been pulled into a messy state, his tone warm yet refusing refusal: "With injuries like this, someone will worry."

~~~
